name: India Spice
lede: India Spice is a brownish orange from the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930, one of the most common colors in our painting archive despite a name that points to no documented pigment or dye.

sections.title: A 1930 name, no pigment attached
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates this color's first recording to 1927, on plate 13 B 8, and gives it an alternate name, Toasted Almond, in the same entry [1]. No ISCC-NBS block is recorded for this chip in our library, and neither source says which spice, or which part of India, the name is meant to evoke [1]. In Munsell terms it reads 6.2YR 5.3/6.2, a warm, moderately saturated orange-brown [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[cork]] and [[mikado-brown]], at 2.8 and 3.5 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to this color in 1,945 of 23,781 paintings, about 8.18 percent, and in 1,267 by the stricter within-painting measure, more common than 92 percent of the named colors we track [2]. Inside those paintings it most often sits as an accent, 61 percent of the 1,267 [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1300s, at 2.2 times the expected rate, and is most over-represented in paintings from India itself, at 2.1 times expected, 54 of 721 such paintings, and in Mughal court paintings specifically, at 2.8 times expected [2]. Andre Derain is its most devoted painter here, present in 7 of his 22 works in the archive, 2.9 to 4.2 times the baseline [2].

The earliest match in our archive dates to the year 1100, with the latest from 1936, 1,133 dated paintings in all, 830 years before the name's own earliest record, 1930 [1], a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [1][2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
